page.layout: One page of text in a single main column; a handwritten note block in the right margin (manuscript annotations, not printed text, described under notes). Running head at top left and centre, page number and chapter label at top right. Ornament band, then centred headings, then the body text.

main_text.l: CAPUT SECUNDUM.
DE PRINCIPIIS
AC CAVSIS
NOSTRA SENTENTIA.
SECTIO PRIMA.
I. Notio ac vis vocabuli Principij in vulgato loquendi
usu. Principium & Initium, idem. II. Suarezij flu-
ctuationes, super primaria ac vulgata hujus vocis no-
tione. Primus in ordine loci non recte dicitur Princi-
pium eorum, qui post ipsum: III. Ita neq; Primogenitus,
Principium dicendus reliquorum liberorum.
Hebraica vox Reschith, multo latius patet, quam Graeca
ἀρχὴ, aut Latina Principium. IV. Philosophicus vocis Prin-
cipij usus, incertissimus apud Aristotelem, atq; ad
plurimas diversissimas res promiscue accommodatus.
V. Enumeratio significationum hujus vocabuli, non
rite facta ab Aristotele in initio quinti Metaphysico-
rum. VI. Ineptissimus Aristotelicorum conatus, ad
distorquendum illud magistri sui dictum, ubi
conceptis verbis fatetur, Causam & Principium reciproce dici.
VII. Censura Aristotelis, super isto vocum abusu vaga.

page.notes: Handwritten manuscript annotations in the right margin (English-style notes in pen, partly illegible) and interlinear pencil or ink marks above the text are not printed and are not transcribed. Several printed words in the text carry small superscript corrections (e.g. "Usus", "Employ", "inconstantissimus", "synonymia") that are manuscript insertions. Greek words in the text transcribed as best read; the accents may be imperfect.
